A release is a set of files produced by one version of the OPDI software, with one set of names and meanings. Every row says which release it belongs to, in its column release. Older releases are on the Roadmap.

title: Releases
section: What is new in release v2.0.0
text:
What is new in release v2.0.0

One file per day, and events with their measurements
Release v2.0.0 has two files per day:

the flight list, one row per flight, and
the flight events, one row per event, with the event’s measurements as columns, and the columns of its flight.

A measurement no longer needs a join to its event, and an event no longer needs a join to its flight. The separate measurements files are no longer produced. A day’s files hold the flights first seen that day, with all their events, also those after midnight (see Data).


Worldwide coverage
Release v2.0.0 covers every flight the OpenSky Network received, anywhere in the world.


More event types
Release v2.0.0 adds these event families, all listed on the Data dictionary.

Runway milestones: start of the take-off roll, take-off (ATOT), passage over the runway threshold (xing-runway-threshold), touchdown (ALDT), line-up, runway vacated, runway crossings and go-arounds.
Block times: off-block (AOBT) and in-block (AIBT), when the aircraft leaves and reaches its parking position.
Distance rings: crossings of circles of 40 to 120 NM around the departure and destination airports.
Level-offs: periods of level flight during the climb and the descent.
Holding: start and end of each holding pattern, with its duration, distance and number of loops.
Point merge: the legs of point merge arrival procedures, with their time and distance.
FIR crossings: each passage from one flight information region to the next.



A richer flight list
The flight list holds the main times of each flight, copied from its events: take-off and landing, off-block and in-block, the runways and stands used and the times of crossing the distance rings. It also says how each airport was decided (adep_source, ades_source) and whether a row counts as a departure or an arrival (movement_dep, movement_arr). Column names are in lower case.


One flight across a reception gap
When an aircraft is out of range of every receiver for more than 30 minutes, for example over an ocean, release v0.0.2 started a new flight after the gap. Release v2.0.0 keeps one flight when the data on both sides fit one continuous flight (see Track identity). Long flights are therefore more often one row, with both airports.


Other changes

Cleaner positions: repeated, impossible and isolated values are removed before any event is detected (see Trajectory cleaning).
Documented and checked methods: each has a page in Algorithms on how it works, what it was compared with, how accurate it is and where it fails. Data quality gives how often every item exists and how close it is to the records, overall and per airport.
Trino: the files can be queried with SQL on the OpenSky Network’s Trino instance, without downloading them (see Access).

Flight list: for each flight, the aircraft address (ICAO24), call sign (FLT_ID), date of flight (DOF), departure and destination airports (ADEP, ADES), other possible airports (ADEP_P, ADES_P), data on the aircraft and the first and last time it was seen.
Event: a moment in a flight, with a time, a position and an altitude in feet. flight_id links it to the flight list’s ID.
Measurement: a value attached to an event, the distance flown (type = Distance flown (NM)) or the time passed (type = Time Passed (s)) since the start of the flight. event_id links it to the event’s id.
The airport and runway tables are a selection of the OurAirports columns.

The position reports of a flight can be fetched from the OpenSky Network’s historical database with ICAO24, the call sign and the time from FIRST_SEEN to LAST_SEEN, for example with the tools on its data tools page.



Download scripts
Each file has its own web address:
https://www.eurocontrol.int/performance/data/download/OPDI/v002/flight_list/flight_list_{YYYYMM}.parquet
https://www.eurocontrol.int/performance/data/download/OPDI/v002/flight_events/flight_events_{YYYYMMDD}_{YYYYMMDD}.parquet
https://www.eurocontrol.int/performance/data/download/OPDI/v002/measurements/measurements_{YYYYMMDD}_{YYYYMMDD}.parquet
YYYYMM is the year and month. In the ten-day files, the first date is the first day of the period and the second the day after its last day. Periods start on 1 January 2022 and follow each other every ten days.
The scripts download every file of the release into a folder data/. Change the dates in periods to download less.






Python download script





import os
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

import requests
from dateutil.relativedelta import relativedelta

BASE = "https://www.eurocontrol.int/performance/data/download/OPDI/v002"


def generate_urls(data_type: str, start: str, end: str) -> list:
    """Addresses of the files of one kind between two dates.

    data_type: "flight_list" (monthly files, dates as YYYYMM), or
    "flight_events" or "measurements" (ten-day files, dates as YYYYMMDD).
    The ten-day files start on 1 January 2022 and every ten days after it.
    """
    urls = []
    if data_type == "flight_list":
        current = datetime.strptime(start, "%Y%m")
        last = datetime.strptime(end, "%Y%m")
        while current <= last:
            urls.append(f"{BASE}/{data_type}/{data_type}_{current:%Y%m}.parquet")
            current += relativedelta(months=1)
    else:
        current = datetime.strptime(start, "%Y%m%d")
        last = datetime.strptime(end, "%Y%m%d")
        while current < last:
            following = current + timedelta(days=10)
            urls.append(f"{BASE}/{data_type}/{data_type}_{current:%Y%m%d}_{following:%Y%m%d}.parquet")
            current = following
    return urls


def download_files(urls: list, folder: str) -> None:
    """Download the files into a folder, skipping files already there."""
    os.makedirs(folder, exist_ok=True)
    for url in urls:
        path = os.path.join(folder, url.split("/")[-1])
        if os.path.exists(path):
            print(f"Skipping {path}, already there.")
            continue
        print(f"Downloading {url} ...")
        try:
            response = requests.get(url, stream=True)
            response.raise_for_status()
            with open(path, "wb") as handle:
                for chunk in response.iter_content(chunk_size=1024 * 1024):
                    handle.write(chunk)
        except requests.exceptions.RequestException as error:
            print(f"Failed to download {url}: {error}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    periods = {
        "flight_list": ("202201", "202609"),
        "flight_events": ("20220101", "20260930"),
        "measurements": ("20220101", "20260930"),
    }
    for data_type, (start, end) in periods.items():
        download_files(generate_urls(data_type, start, end), f"./data/{data_type}")









R download script





library(httr)
library(lubridate)
library(fs)

base <- "https://www.eurocontrol.int/performance/data/download/OPDI/v002"

# Addresses of the files of one kind between two dates.
# data_type: "flight_list" (monthly files, dates as YYYYMM), or
# "flight_events" or "measurements" (ten-day files, dates as YYYYMMDD).
# The ten-day files start on 1 January 2022 and every ten days after it.
generate_urls <- function(data_type, start, end) {
  urls <- character(0)
  if (data_type == "flight_list") {
    current <- ymd(paste0(start, "01"))
    last <- ymd(paste0(end, "01"))
    while (current <= last) {
      urls <- c(urls, sprintf("%s/%s/%s_%s.parquet", base, data_type, data_type,
                              format(current, "%Y%m")))
      current <- current %m+% months(1)
    }
  } else {
    current <- ymd(start)
    last <- ymd(end)
    while (current < last) {
      following <- current + days(10)
      urls <- c(urls, sprintf("%s/%s/%s_%s_%s.parquet", base, data_type, data_type,
                              format(current, "%Y%m%d"), format(following, "%Y%m%d")))
      current <- following
    }
  }
  urls
}

# Download the files into a folder, skipping files already there.
download_files <- function(urls, folder) {
  dir_create(folder)
  for (url in urls) {
    path <- file.path(folder, basename(url))
    if (file_exists(path)) {

How release v0.0.2 was computed
An earlier version of the OPDI software produced release v0.0.2. Its methods differ from those in Algorithms, which apply to release v2.0.0.

Flights and their identifiers
The position reports of the OpenSky Network (state vectors) were grouped by aircraft address (icao24) and call sign. A group was split into separate flights where two consecutive reports were more than 30 minutes apart, or more than 10 minutes apart while the aircraft was below 1 km. Each flight got an identifier made of the SHA-256 hash of the address and call sign, a sequence number, and the year and month.


Departure and destination airports
A circle of 30 NM radius around every airport was filled with H3 cells of resolution 7. H3 divides the Earth into hexagonal cells; these cover about 5 km² each. Only reports below 4,000 ft were kept, and each was matched to the airports whose circle contains its cell. The airport nearest to the first (or last) matching report became the departure (or destination) airport; the other candidates went into ADEP_P (or ADES_P).


Flight events







Event type
Meaning




level-start, level-end
Start and end of a level segment.


top-of-climb
First report of the first cruise phase.


top-of-descent
Last report of the last cruise phase.


take-off
First report of the climb phase after a ground phase.


landing
First report of the ground phase after a descent phase.


first-xing-fl50, first-xing-fl70, first-xing-fl100, first-xing-fl245
First crossing of flight level 50, 70, 100 or 245.


last-xing-fl50, last-xing-fl70, last-xing-fl100, last-xing-fl245
Last crossing of that flight level.


entry-runway, exit-runway
Entry into and exit from a runway.


entry-taxiway, exit-taxiway
Entry into and exit from a taxiway.


entry-parking_position, exit-parking_position
Entry into and exit from a parking position (stand).



The flight phases (ground, climb, cruise, level, descent) came from the fuzzy logic of OpenAP, an open aircraft performance model by Junzi Sun of TU Delft. For the flight-level crossings, a smoothed flight level was computed for each report and compared between consecutive reports. Airport areas (runways, taxiways, parking positions) came from OpenStreetMap, filled with H3 cells of resolution 12, and each report was matched to them. The info field of the airport events holds the OpenStreetMap details of the area, as JSON text.


Measurements

Distance flown (NM): the great-circle distance between consecutive reports, added up from the first report of the flight, in nautical miles.
Time Passed (s): the time since the first report of the flight, in seconds.

Each event got the two values of the report it was taken from.

For questions about these files, contact pru-support@eurocontrol.int.

References of the algorithms
The published work, standards, software and data that the Algorithms pages name under Based on. Each page says how its method relates to them: taken from a source, derived in part from it, or comparable to it but developed separately.
Standards and EUROCONTROL methods

EUROCONTROL (2017). Airport Collaborative Decision-Making (A-CDM) Implementation Manual, version 5.0, 31 March 2017. Publication page. Defines the 16 A-CDM milestones, among them landing (ALDT, milestone 6), in-block (AIBT, 7), off-block (AOBT, 15) and take-off (ATOT, 16), and the taxi-out and taxi-in times.
ICAO. GANP Portal: KPI overview (the key performance indicators of the Global Air Navigation Plan). PDF. Among them KPI02 (taxi-out additional time), KPI05 (actual en-route extension), KPI08 (additional time in terminal airspace, with 40 NM and 100 NM cylinders), KPI13 (taxi-in additional time), KPI17 (level-off during climb) and KPI19 (level-off during descent).
Peeters, S., and Guastalla, G. (2017). Analysis of vertical flight efficiency during climb and descent. EUROCONTROL Performance Review Unit, edition 00-04, 19 January 2017. PDF.
EUROCONTROL. Point Merge (concept page, with the reference documents of the method). Web page.
EUROCONTROL (2026). Point Merge catalogue: an inventory of worldwide implementations, July 2026. Publication page.
AirNav Ireland. Irish AIP, ENR 1.5 Holding, approach and departure procedures (AIRAC 14 May 2026). States that holding procedures are based on ICAO Doc 8168 (PANS-OPS), Volume II. Web page.

title: Resources
text:
OPDI Software
Open-source projects created and maintained by the Performance Review Commission (PRC) as part of the initiative.


Python
OPDI
The software that produces the OPDI data: a Python package that runs the processing steps on Apache Spark, from the OpenSky Network’s position reports to the published daily files. Processing steps describes what it does, and the Algorithms pages describe each algorithm.
 Repository ·  API reference




Python
OPDI reader (opdi.published)
A small part of the OPDI package that reads the published daily files into pandas tables, gives back the table shapes of release v0.0.2, and creates DuckDB views. It needs pandas, pyarrow and DuckDB, not Spark. See Access for examples.
 Repository




Airflow
OPDI daily processing (Airflow)
The schedule that produces the data: two Apache Airflow workflows, one that processes each new day and one that processes a chosen range of past days. They are in the airflow/ folder of the OPDI repository, with instructions for running them.
 Repository




Python
HexAeroPy
Determines the airports, runways, taxiways, and stands used by a flight from its coordinates alone. Developed for small-scale applications of the OPDI approach to airport layouts.
 Repository
